summary: Provision ephemeral reviewer groups, Confluence one-click incident-template sync, and Slack thread->Confluence export bot
description:
Issue summary: We need an automated admin workflow to create timebound reviewer groups scoped to a Jira project and a Confluence space for post-incident reviews, plus a Slack channel integration that can export highlighted threads (thread root + selected replies) into a new Confluence page using the incident template.

Impact: Currently, post-incident reviews are manual: owners create groups, copy Slack threads into Confluence, and manually confirm access. This adds friction, delays retros, and causes inconsistent audit trails for compliance. Target users are SREs, oncall, CS, and legal reviewers.

Request: 1) A self-service Jira admin action (button) that provisions an ephemeral G-Suite/SCIM group named "incident-<jira-key>-reviewers" with TTL (default 30 days) and membership seeded from a multi-select in the ticket; 2) Confluence space template sync so that the exported Slack thread uses the canonical incident template and is created in a specified space with permissions set to the ephemeral group; 3) A Slack app/automation (or enable existing bot) that adds a channel action "Export thread to Confluence" visible to channel owners and oncall, which gathers the thread root + chosen replies, converts to template sections, and attaches metadata (jira key, reviewer group, export timestamp).

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Background: Compliance asked for tamper-evident review artifacts for incidents involving PII or customer-affecting outages. We piloted a manual process in #postmortems that worked but is high-friction. Infra should ensure SRP (scoped-role permissions) and audit logs are available, and TTLs auto-revoke group membership.

Proposed design notes: Use SCIM provisioning to create the group and set expiry; Confluence REST API to create page from template and set page restrictions to the group; Slack app should call a secured endpoint that validates the requesting user's role and the Jira key context, then post to Confluence and return a link. Use existing infra oauth service and log events to an ops-audit log.

Dependencies: SCIM provisioning access, Confluence template id (ops-incident-template), Slack app install permissions in workspace, and a short-lived credentials mechanism for the bot.

Risks: Incorrectly scoping page permissions could expose sensitive data; TTL revoke must be robust.
acceptance_criteria: Admin button in Jira that creates a group named incident-<jira-key>-reviewers and records TTL metadata
Group created via SCIM with initial members matching the Jira multi-select and auto-removal after TTL
Confluence export creates a page using the ops incident template and sets view/edit restrictions to the ephemeral group
Slack channel action available that calls the export flow and returns a Confluence link in-channel
All actions are logged to ops-audit and show the initiating user, timestamp, and Jira key
Documentation added to Confluence describing the flow and how to revoke groups before TTL
comments: Maya Chen (2026-03-14): Filing this to reduce manual overhead for postmortems and satisfy compliance evidence requirements. Prefer default TTL of 30 days but want it configurable per-ticket.

Liam O'Rourke (Infra) (2026-03-15): Question — do we have an existing SCIM integration that allows TTL metadata, or do we need an external scheduler to remove members? Also need to confirm which Confluence space (ops or legal) should host the pages.

Maya Chen (2026-03-15): We don't currently have TTL metadata on groups; scheduler approach is acceptable. Default target space: OPS (https://confluence.redwood.ai/spaces/OPS). Legal may request copies via watcher notifications.
investigation_notes: Checked existing SCIM connector (identity-redwood) — supports group create/delete via API but no native TTL field. Plan: store expiry as group attribute in our metadata DB and run periodic cleanup lambda.
Found existing Confluence template 'ops-incident-template' at https://confluence.redwood.ai/spaces/OPS/pages/12345 - needs minor adjustments to accept Slack export fields.

Slack app 'export-bot' exists in org but currently only posts ephemeral messages and cannot create Confluence pages. PR required to extend scope and add Confluence credentials vault usage. See related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/pull/2828
notes: Prefers a minimal MVP that uses the group cleanup lambda and a bot extension; can iterate on UI polish. If Legal wants copies longer than TTL we should add an export-to-archive workflow.
